claims.text: RHEA–Cu composite structures have a significant positive heat of mixing between Cu and the refractory alloying elements.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials used in molecular dynamics simulations can facilitate the design of large-scale reactions and stable RHEA–Cu microstructures.
The machine-learning interatomic potentials can accurately predict the thermodynamic properties of the RHEA–Cu system.
The machine-learning interatomic potentials can accurately predict the kinetic properties of the RHEA–Cu system.
The interatomic-potential training dataset is based on DFT calculations.
The proposed simulations apply at temperatures from 500 to 1000 K.
The relevant predicted thermodynamic and kinetic properties include phase diagrams, diffusion coefficients, and defect formation energies.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can accurately capture the complex interactions between Cu and refractory alloying elements.
Capturing those interactions permits prediction of stable microstructures.
Capturing those interactions permits prediction of large-scale reaction kinetics.
The intervention will increase microstructure stability by 20% relative to commonly used composite-forming methods.
Microstructure stability can be measured through reductions in defect formation energies.
The intervention will increase the reaction rate by 30% relative to commonly used composite-forming methods.
Reaction-rate improvement can be measured through increases in diffusion coefficients.
Commonly used methods for forming composite structures are insufficient because of the positive heat-of-mixing issue.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potentials is limited by the accuracy of the training dataset.
The scale or performance of the MD simulations is limited by available computational resources.
Experimental data available for validating predictions in this alloy system are limited.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies 20% greater stability and 30% greater reaction rate, but the falsification rule uses lower thresholds of 10% and 20%. Thus, results below the stated predictions could nevertheless avoid falsification.
